newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Francophone agency pledges aid for Hanoi summit.
newsitem.headline: Francophone agency pledges aid for Hanoi summit.

text.p: The body responsible for cooperation between Francophone countries said on Saturday it had pledged 14.59 million French francs ($2.86 million) to Hanoi as host of the seventh summit of its members in November 1997.

Jean-Louis Roy, secretary general of the Agence de la Francophonie, told reporters that more than a third of the funds would be spent on preparations for the summit and the rest was destined for cooperation projects such as education and training.
La Francophonie is a loose association of 47 nations grouping some 400 million people around the globe.
It has traditionally been seen as a forum for keeping French in the race with English as the international language of trade, technology and communications.
Communist Vietnam's collective memory of its era as a French colony, which ended in 1954, is waning fast and less than 0.1 percent of its 75 million people can speak French competently.
Nevertheless, the Agence de la Francophonie argues that its mission is not to defend the French language but to nurture cooperation and a common vision between its members.
"La Francophonie is not there to fight against a language," Roy said. "For me monolingualism went out at the end of the 19th century."

France said earlier this year that it had provided 70 percent of the 100 million French franc ($19.6 million) cost of last year's summit, in the African state of Benin, and was ready to put up just as much for the Hanoi summit.
Paris has agreed to sponsor renovation of the now dilapidated Hanoi Opera House, where news conferences and a grand gala evening will be held during the summit.
